'''Sujoy Kumar Guha''' is an Indian [[biomedical engineering|biomedical engineer]]. He was born in Patna, India, 20 June 1940.<ref name=iitkgp>[http://www.iitkgp.ac.in/top-awardees/daa1.php?Sl=73 Distinguished Alumnus of IIT Kharagpur] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411033855/http://www.iitkgp.ac.in/top-awardees/daa1.php?Sl=73 |date=11 April 2016 }}, retrieved 2015-04-23.</ref> He did his undergraduate degree (''B.Tech.'') in [[electrical engineering]] from [[IIT Kharagpur]], followed by a master's degree in electrical engineering at IIT, and another [[master's degree]] from the [[University of Illinois]], Urbana-Champaign. Guha later received his [[PhD]] in medical [[physiology]] from [[Saint Louis University (United States)|St. Louis University]].<ref name=wired>{{cite web|last=Gifford|first=Bill|title=The Revolutionary New Birth Control Method for Men|url=https://www.wired.com/2011/04/ff-vasectomy/|work=Wired May 2011|publisher=Wired Magazine|access-date=2012-05-31}}</ref>

Guha founded the Centre for Biomedical Engineering. He obtained his [[Bachelors of Medicine and Surgery|MBBS]] degree from the [[University College of Medical Sciences]], [[Delhi University]]. One of the founders of biomedical engineering in India, Guha is internationally known in the areas of [[Physical therapy|rehabilitation]] engineering, [[bioengineering]] in reproductive medicine, and technology for rural health care. He has received several [[award]]s and has more than 100 research papers in cited journals. In 2003, he became a chair professor at IIT Kharagpur.<ref name=iitkgp/> He was awarded the [[Padma Shri]], India's fourth-highest civilian honor in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Padma Awards | url=https://padmaawards.gov.in/PDFS/2020AwardeesList.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125153324/https://padmaawards.gov.in/PDFS/2020AwardeesList.pdf | archive-date=2020-01-25}}</ref>

Guha's major contributions have been in the invention and development of the non-hormonal polymer-based injectable [[male contraceptive]] ([[RISUG]]), for which the final Phase III clinical trials were completed in 2019.<ref name=wired/><ref>{{cite web|last=Kaul|first=Rhythma|title=India closer to world's first male contraceptive injection|date=19 November 2019 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-closer-to-world-s-first-male-contraceptive-injection/story-o3lTFLnCkKHpuEDNNqrEnO.html|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=2020-08-30}}</ref>
